seo_title: How to Prepare for Your Food Tour
seo_description: Prepare for your Simply Enak food tour in Malaysia. What to wear, what to bring, dietary notes, and what to expect.
hero_title: How to Prepare for Your Food Tour
hero_description: A few practical tips to help you get the most out of your Simply Enak food tour.

whatToExpect.title: Small group size
whatToExpect.description: Tours are kept to 12 people max. You get personal attention and can actually hear your guide at busy stalls.

whatToExpect.title: 3-4 hours of eating
whatToExpect.description: Expect to stop at 6-8 tasting points. Come hungry — the portions add up to a full meal and then some.

whatToExpect.title: Lots of walking
whatToExpect.description: Most tours cover 1-2 km on foot, mostly in backlanes and markets. Pace is relaxed with plenty of stops to eat and listen.

whatToExpect.title: Rain or shine
whatToExpect.description: Tours run in all weather. Markets have cover but you will get wet. That is part of the experience.

whatToExpect.title: Your guide orders for you
whatToExpect.description: No menus, no decisions. Your guide picks the best dishes at each stop. Just say if you cannot eat something.

dietary_intro: Tell us about any dietary needs when you book. We accommodate vegetarian, vegan, halal, gluten-free, and Jain diets on every tour.

dietary_notes.title: Vegetarian & vegan
dietary_notes.description: Malaysia has strong Indian vegetarian and Chinese vegan traditions. You will eat well.

dietary_notes.title: Halal
dietary_notes.description: All our tours are halal-friendly. We avoid non-halal establishments and point out what to watch for.

dietary_notes.title: Gluten-free
dietary_notes.description: Rice is the base of most dishes. We avoid wheat-based sauces and let you know which dishes are safe.

dietary_notes.title: Allergies
dietary_notes.description: Severe allergies are hard to manage in street-food settings. We will be honest about risk at each stop.
